Thermal designSummer 2026

Hydrogen Peroxide Tank
Thermal Management

Manastu Space Technologies · Internship

A passive cooling concept connecting a spacecraft propellant tank to an external radiator through an aluminum saddle and heat pipes.

  • Fusion 360
  • Excel
  • Heat transfer
Read project

My contribution

I sized the tank using the usable propellant requirement and blowdown conditions, then modelled the tank, saddle, heat pipes, and radiator in Fusion 360. Rounded tank ends and a cylindrical middle section provided room for mounting and thermal contact.

Engineering approach

I assessed heat transfer through tube connections and radiation to the spacecraft, and considered sunlight and Earth radiation at the radiator. A thermal-resistance model connected the full heat-transfer path to geometry, contact areas, and interface materials. The saddle used a removable mechanical interface with the tank.

Outcome

I produced a CAD concept and technical report supporting preliminary hot-case feasibility. Hardware performance and cold-case control still required verification. The work helped me connect thermal calculations with mechanical packaging and identify assumptions that needed confirmation.

Mechanical integrationSummer 2026

Xenon Tank Packaging
& Feasibility

Manastu Space Technologies · Internship

A compact electric-propulsion assembly, paired with a real-fluid pressure assessment of xenon storage across the operating temperature range.

  • SolidWorks
  • NIST fluid data
  • Excel
Read project

My contribution

I designed the support structure and assembled the tank, electrical boxes, thruster, and cathode in SolidWorks. The layout secured the vertical tank with clamps, positioned electrical boxes alongside it, and mounted the thruster and cathode above the tank.

Engineering approach

I developed the mounting interfaces and produced a drawing with dimensioned orthographic views, an isometric view, and a bill of materials. I then used the required xenon mass and tank volume to establish bulk density, obtained real-fluid data from the NIST Chemistry WebBook, and plotted pressure against temperature in Excel.

Outcome

The CAD assembly, engineering drawing, and feasibility report linked the packaging concept to its operating requirements. Comparing the highest predicted equilibrium pressure with the stated tank rating supported the proposed storage conditions on an equilibrium basis.

SimulationSummer 2026

Solenoid Modelling
in ANSYS Maxwell

Manastu Space Technologies · Internship

  • SolidWorks
  • ANSYS Maxwell 3D
  • Magnetostatics

A CAD-to-simulation workflow for a solenoid, building skills relevant to magnetic-circuit analysis for Hall-effect thrusters.

Read project

My contribution

I modelled the coil and core in SolidWorks, using a helical path and swept profile for the coil. I maintained clearance between the separate bodies, prepared flat terminal faces, and exported the geometry to Maxwell as a STEP file.

Engineering approach

I set up a magnetostatic analysis, assigned materials and current terminals, and created the surrounding region. Troubleshooting focused on body clearance, terminal alignment with the region boundary, and current-path validation. After solving, I examined flux-density magnitude and vector plots to understand the field distribution and direction.

Outcome

I produced field visualizations and a workflow report for knowledge transfer. The task also clarified the difference between obtaining a successful solution and quantitatively validating it through analytical comparisons, mesh checks, and boundary-sensitivity studies.

University projects

McGill University · Winter 2026

ThermodynamicsWinter 2026

Geothermal Power Plant
& Heat Recovery

McGill University · MECH 341 · Group project

A geothermal generation study for Mongolia's Bayankhongor region, with a heat-pump concept to recover condenser heat for heating.

  • MATLAB
  • Cycle analysis
  • Technical research
Read project

My contribution

I contributed to evaluating geothermal generation against a methane-fuelled Rankine-cycle baseline and comparing environmental implications. I also developed a concept for using a heat pump to raise low-temperature condenser heat to a useful level for residential or district heating.

Engineering approach

Our group compared the baseline steam cycle with a proposed double-flash geothermal plant at Shargaljuut, bringing together cycle calculations, infrastructure needs, and economic and environmental considerations. My heat-recovery assessment accounted for the additional compressor electricity demand alongside the plant's local electrical loads.

Outcome

The group concept met the modelled baseload target, with additional capacity needed for peak demand. Heat recovery offered a potential use for condenser heat, subject to available electricity. The project connected thermodynamic performance with practical power-generation and heating decisions.

Design for manufacturingWinter 2026

C-Clamp Design
& Manufacturing

McGill University · MECH 360 · Group project

A manufacturing demonstrator taking a clamp and its mould components from CAD to 3D printing, CNC milling, turning, and assembly.

  • SolidWorks
  • Mastercam
  • CNC machining
  • 3D printing
Read project

My contribution

I contributed to the SolidWorks parts and assembly and to milling and turning toolpaths in Mastercam. Our team made a printed clamp body, a turned side-action component, and two milled foam mould halves, updating related models and toolpaths as the design evolved.

Engineering approach

We adapted corners, clearances, and mould features to cutter sizes, tool access, and available stock. A flat printing surface reduced supports, while the mould layout let us machine both halves from one block. We omitted threading because the required tooling was unavailable, using unthreaded mating components for the demonstrator.

Outcome

The components fitted together after finishing work. Foam surface finish and manual mould separation remained limitations. The project strengthened my understanding of manufacturing constraints and how a change to one part affects the complete assembly.
